hints: Use the drawn condition x=2 in the circle (x−3)²+(y−1)²=4.
Choose the lower intersection shown for P and state it as x+iy with an exact surd.
walkthrough:
Write the equation of the circle $|z - (3 + \mathrm{i})| = 2$ in Cartesian form with $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$:
$$(x - 3)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 2^2 = 4$$

Substitute the vertical boundary line $x = 2$ into the circle equation:
$$(2 - 3)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 4$$
$$(-1)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 4 \implies 1 + (y - 1)^2 = 4$$
$$(y - 1)^2 = 3 \implies y - 1 = \pm\sqrt{3} \implies y = 1 \pm \sqrt{3}$$

Select the lower intersection point $P$ shown on the Argand diagram:
$$y = 1 - \sqrt{3} \quad (\text{since } 1 - \sqrt{3} < 1 + \sqrt{3})$$

Express the complex number $P$ in exact Cartesian form $x + \mathrm{i}y$:
$$z = 2 + (1 - \sqrt{3})\mathrm{i} \quad (\text{or } 2 - (\sqrt{3} - 1)\mathrm{i})$$

hints: The greatest argument is the tangent ray from the origin to the circle bounding the shaded region.
Add the centre's angle tan⁻¹(1/3) to the tangent angle sin⁻¹(2/√10), then report the result to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Identify that the greatest value of $\arg z$ occurs along the upper tangent from the origin to the circle $|z - (3 + \mathrm{i})| = 2$:
$$\text{Center of the circle: } C(3, 1), \quad \text{Radius: } R = 2$$

Calculate the distance from the origin $O(0, 0)$ to the center $C(3, 1)$:
$$OC = \sqrt{3^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{9 + 1} = \sqrt{10}$$

Calculate the angle of the line $OC$ with the positive real axis:
$$\theta_1 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) \approx 18.4349^{\circ} \quad (\text{or } 0.32175 \text{ radians})$$

In the right-angled triangle formed by the origin, the center $C$, and the point of contact $T$, calculate the angle $\phi = \angle COT$:
$$\sin\phi = \dfrac{R}{OC} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{10}}$$
$$\phi = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{10}}\right) \approx 39.2315^{\circ} \quad (\text{or } 0.68472 \text{ radians})$$

Verify that the point of contact $T$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re}(z) \leqslant 2$:
$$OT = \sqrt{OC^2 - R^2} = \sqrt{10 - 4} = \sqrt{6} \approx 2.44949$$
$$x_T = OT\cos(\theta_1 + \phi) = 2.44949 \times \cos(57.666^{\circ}) \approx 2.44949 \times 0.53484 \approx 1.31 \leqslant 2$$
$$\text{Thus the tangent touches within the shaded region.}$$

Calculate the greatest value of $\arg z$:
$$\arg z = \theta_1 + \phi = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) + \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{10}}\right)$$
$$\arg z \approx 18.4349^{\circ} + 39.2315^{\circ} = 57.6664^{\circ} \approx 57.7^{\circ} \quad (\text{or } 1.01 \text{ radians})$$
